New Technologies.title: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents

New Technologies.title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling

New Technologies.title: FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis
New Technologies.description: New method for AI terminal task synthesis that preserves both source intent and executable state. Addresses the challenge of maintaining semantic meaning when AI agents automate terminal commands and system operations.

New Technologies.title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models

New Technologies.title: Metrics That Write Themselves: Evolving an Evaluator from Its Own Blind Spots

New Technologies.title: DentAgent: Evidence-Centric Multi-Agent Coordination for Multimodal Dental Reasoning

New Technologies.title: SkillGate: Training In-Policy Skill Selection in Long-Horizon Agents
New Technologies.description: Novel approach for training skill selection in long-horizon AI agents. SkillGate enables agents to select and execute appropriate skills across extended task sequences, addressing a key challenge in agentic AI.

New Technologies.title: ORBITER: Conflict-Aware Decision-Making for Agentic Last-Mile Delivery

New Technologies.title: Tuning the Stochastic Machine: A Systems Engineer's Operating Model for Human-AI Engineering

New Technologies.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

New Technologies.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning

New Technologies.title: What is Missing from AI Post-Training: An Empirical Analysis

New Technologies.title: MLREF: Efficient Module Reuse for Reward Design in Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models
New Technologies.description: Novel approach using LLMs for efficient module reuse in reward design for reinforcement learning. MLREF leverages large language models to identify and reuse successful reward modules across different RL tasks.

New Technologies.title: To Go Far, Go Together: Diverse Preferences Induce a Curriculum for Reward Optimization

New Technologies.title: RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training

New Technologies.title: Why write code in 2026

(2) Claude's hourly rate is ~$17, comparable to some human workers, but may rise as human engineers are 'Ubered away'. (3) LLMs can write complex code like Prolog interpreters in WebAssembly successfully. (4) AI tools compress development timelines but don't eliminate the need for developers who understand fundamentals. (5) The distinction between 'software prompters' who use AI for everything vs developers who use AI as a tool.

New Technologies.title: Coding agents have replaced every framework I used

(3) Concern about 'vibe coding' leading to unmaintainable codebases when AI hits limitations. (4) AI productivity gains: some report 10x improvements, others minimal benefit. (5) Frameworks provide shared mental models and patterns that AI-generated bespoke code lacks. (6) Real-world experiment: team used prompts to replace legacy system but abandoned it after months due to complexity and token costs. (7) Determinism argument: compilers are deterministic, LLMs are not - you can't reliably verify AI code without understanding it.

Others.description: New integration with Google Workspace including Gmail for email management, Google Drive for file access and organization, and Google Calendar for scheduling capabilities.

Others.title: LaraCopilot
